post.description: Returns a list of events based on specified time ranges and filtering criteria. This endpoint uses field projection, returning only the specific event attributes requested in the fields parameter.

parameters.name: orgId
parameters.description: ID of your ControlUp organization. You can find your organization ID on the [API Key Management page](how-to-make-api-requests#how-to-find-your-controlup-organization-id) in the DEX platform.

200.description: Successfully retrieved events list with cursor-based pagination

data.description: Array of events on the current page. The event fields returned depends on the `fields` parameter.

nextCursor.description: Base64-encoded cursor for the next page. Null if this is the last page.

previousCursor.description: Base64-encoded cursor for the previous page. Null if this is the first page.

pageSize.description: Number of items in the current page.

401.description: Unauthorized - Invalid or missing authentication token

403.description: Forbidden: Access to this resource is denied

500.description: Internal Server Error - Unexpected server error

get.description: Returns the count of unique values (cardinality) for a specified field within a defined time range. This endpoint allows you to quantify the diversity of your event data such as counting unique users, distinct error types, or total event volume, while applying filters to narrow the scope.

parameters.name: filters
parameters.description:
To use the filter builder, you must first select a single top-level logic group (AND/OR) and then add your filter conditions within the group. All conditions in the group are evaluated together using the group's logic operator (AND/OR).

Do not include both operator types at the top-level. If you need to combine AND/OR logic, you can switch the logic type by adding a new nested group object within the first group, such as AND[user is Bob, OR[severity is high, severity is low]]. This translates to "user is Bob AND (severity is high OR severity is low)".

Note that you can also send the filter object as a JSON-encoded string. Ensure your JSON follows the same structure as the query builder.

and.description: Array of filters/groups where ALL conditions must match (AND logic)

op.description:
Comparison operator.
- Use equals/not_equals for exact matches (works with all fields).
- Use contains for partial string matching (only for string fields like name, userName, guestName, sourceName, NOT for severity enum).
- Use greater/less/greater_or_equals/less_or_equals for numeric comparisons.
- Use between for range queries.

value.description: Value to compare against. Can be string, number, or array for between operator.

group.description: A nested AND/OR group. Use group to create complex queries with nested AND/OR logic.

and.description: Array of filters/groups where ALL conditions must match (AND logic)

or.description: Array of filters/groups where ANY condition can match (OR logic)
Array of filters/groups where ANY condition can match (OR logic)

groups.description: A list of groups the source product belongs to.

tags.description: A list of tags associated with the source product.

groupId.description: Identifier for grouping related events together. Events with the same groupId are part of the same logical group or incident.

alertId.description: Identifier of the alert rule that triggered this event. Links the event to its source alert definition.

sourceType.description: Additional source type classification. Provides more granular detail about the source.

severity.description: The severity level of the event: Informational, Low, Medium, High, or Critical.

uuid.description: Unique identifier (UUID) for this event. Primary key used to retrieve the event.

utcOffsetSeconds.description: The UTC offset in seconds for the timezone where the event originated. Used to calculate local time at the source.

userName.description: The username of the employee associated with this event.

type.description: The category or type of the event. Used to classify events into logical groups.

triggerCondition.description: A human-readable description of the conditions that triggered this event. Enriched by AI to provide a clear explanation of thresholds/rules met.
triggerCondition.example: The trigger activates if the CPU load is 90% or more for at least 60 seconds.

timestampUtcMs.description: The timestamp when the event occurred, as Unix epoch time in milliseconds (UTC).

sourceName.description: The ControlUp product/value stream that generated the event. SOURCE_NAME_VDI = VDI, SOURCE_NAME_DESKTOP = Devices, SOURCE_NAME_SYNTHETIC = Synthetic Monitoring.

remoteVirtualSession.description: For VDI environments, the identifier or name of the virtual session associated with this event.

remoteSessionClientIp.description: For remote sessions (VDI/RDP), the IP address of the client machine connecting to the session.

publicIpAddress.description: The public-facing IP address of the device where the event occurred.

ipAddress.description: The private/internal IP address of the device where the event occurred.

name.description: The name/title of the event. Human-readable identifier for what occurred.

hostName.description: The hostname of the machine where the event occurred. For VDI, this is the host server name.

guestName.description: The name of the source device - guest machine/VM or device name where the event originated.

folderPath.description: The file system path relevant to the event.

applicationName.description: The name of the application associated with the event.

additionalData.description: A flexible key-value map containing extra event data. May include device_id, os_version, app_version, or custom metrics.

id.description: Unique identifier of the preset to update

actionUrlParams.description: Map of parameter names to values for action URLs params

fieldsUrlParams.description: Map of parameter names to values for field URL params

op.description:
Comparison operator.
- Use equals/not_equals for exact matches (works with all fields).
- Use contains for partial string matching (only for string fields like name, userName, guestName, sourceName, NOT for severity enum).
- Use greater/less/greater_or_equals/less_or_equals for numeric comparisons.
- Use between for range queries.

value.description: Value to compare against. Can be string or number. For severity field, valid values are: Informational, Low, Medium, High, Critical. For between operator, value should be array with two elements [min, max].
